title: Execute Claude assignments with native identity, team operations and accountable receipts
goal: Make the Claude execution environment a conforming participant in the complete team without copying authentication or guessing native settings and isolation.
scope: Implement ExecutionBackend(Claude) and native discovery/readiness using the actual supported local protocol. Preserve persistent Agent identity, provider version, native session, per-model efforts and requested/sent/reported settings; explicitly retain unknown metadata.

Support admitted prompt/grant/allowance, structured role output, progress, ToolDenied, TeamOperation requests, cancellation/timeout and final Receipt. Normalize input/cache-read/cache-write/output/reasoning usage to A13 without double counting or turning partial counters into complete usage.

Integrate with actual Direct workspace permission enforcement and hidden-context exclusions; add IsolatedCopy enforcement when W4-0001 lands and before W4-0002 uses Claude producers. Map Infrastructure/Environment/Protocol/Content/Unknown failures and unresolved side effects into the recovery path built by W1/W3; do not build a provider-specific acceptance or retry authority.

Provide reproducible native-protocol fixtures through Registry, Gatekeeper and Dispatcher, and document how an explicitly authorized real native run is performed and which observations it can establish.
acceptance: The real Registry/Gatekeeper/Dispatcher consumer executes a Claude protocol fixture with grant-scoped board work and a structured result, preserving native session/profile and normalized receipt; it also completes a producer/reviewer application scenario.

Unsupported setting, denied capability, malformed/foreign operation, duplicate receipt, partial usage and cancellation-with-uncertain-effects cases remain truthful and cannot create extra assignments or acceptance.

Claude and Scripted/Codex exercise the shared backend replacement contract through the actual consumer. Any separately performed native run is labeled separately from fixtures, with exact version and evidence rather than a blanket claim that all Claude environments work.

Scoped cancellation/reattachment fixtures distinguish parent exit or stream loss from validated cessation, retain holds/cost until their independent conditions and do not duplicate execution. Native choices are explicit supported offerings; experiment parameters never invent model/effort support or bypass §3.9/R-19/R-20.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.1/3.4/3.7, 5.1 (ReadinessProbe), 5.7 (ExecutionBackend), A5/A13 and R-2/R-3/R-8/R-9/R-10. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed crates/ymp-runtime/src/backends/claude.rs plus focused native protocol modules and new protocol fixtures. W1-0017 supplies the host/backend contract, W3-0001 team-operation bridge and W4-0001 actual workspace isolation. Build the full Claude adapter here.

Resolve the supported installed/official native protocol during implementation; preserve identity, authentication, native offerings/settings and unknown metadata. Do not copy Codex wire names or effort scales. Build fixture supervision/accounting tests against the common kernel consumer.

Fixtures establish protocol/host behavior and are separate from an explicitly authorized real native run. Scoped cessation, reattachment and independent settlement follow §3.9/R-19/R-20; local build/test grants no inference, installation or real-data mutation authority.

Rescheduled 2026-09-16 into the W3 window: a second model family must exist before W3-0002 (DifferentFamilyComparableStrength), W3-0006 (weaker-judge debate) and the first matched comparisons in W3-0009. The W6 prefix stays because IDs are immutable; scheduling follows dependencies and priority.
